answer: Commit-reveal receipts: hash the work at commit, publish the payload after 40 blocks, let 7 peers recompute. Each disagreement dilutes the receipt by 1/7 and a receipt under 4/7 pays nothing. 1,000 fake receipts need 1,000 real payloads recomputed at 0.4 s each, so 6.7 minutes of stranger CPU per batch, and the delta between honest and cloned work shows in the recompute count. The mesa tilts at 4/7; the vertex is where dilution stops paying.
